lessonRef.title: Concept model B: fitting a function to bivariate data and assessing fit with residual plots

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Compare these two examples. Find the step where they stop being the same.

items.prompt: For ŷ = 4x + 60, interpret the slope where x is hours studied.

steps: Slope is change in y per unit x.
One more hour is associated with about 4 more points.

items.prompt: Ice cream sales correlate with drowning rates. Does ice cream cause drowning?

steps: A lurking variable explains the association.
workedSolution.answer: No; a third variable explains it

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: A data set records 9, 2, 18, 13, 17. Give the mean and the median.
choices: mean 12, median 13
mean 11.8, median 12
mean 13, median 11.8
mean 11.8, median 13

items.prompt: A data set of five values between 10 and 30 has one additional reading of 181 appended. Which statement best describes the effect on the mean and the median?
choices: The mean rises sharply while the median changes little, because the mean uses every value’s size.
Neither statistic changes, because one value cannot affect a summary.
The median rises sharply while the mean changes little.
Both the mean and the median rise sharply.

items.prompt: A two-way table has row 1: 13 yes, 5 no; row 2: 22 yes, 16 no. Among row-1 respondents, what fraction answered yes?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A least-squares line for a data set is ŷ = 2x + 18, where x is measured in hour studieds and y in test points. Interpret the slope.
choices: The predicted value is 2 test points when x is 0.
Each additional hour studied causes an increase of exactly 2 test points.
Each additional test points is associated with 2 more hour studieds.
Each additional hour studied is associated with an increase of about 2 test points.

items.prompt: Towns with more fire engines report more fire damage. What conclusion is justified?
choices: Larger towns have both more engines and more fires, so the association reflects town size rather than a causal link.
Random assignment makes a causal conclusion reasonable, because the groups differ only by the treatment.
A third variable — warm weather — plausibly drives both, so correlation here is not evidence of causation.
A strong correlation always establishes causation when the sample is large.

items.prompt: A data set records 37, 16, 28, 31, 24, 35, 6. Give the mean and the median.
choices: mean 25.29, median 25
mean 25, median 28
mean 28, median 25.29
mean 25.29, median 28

items.prompt: A data set of five values between 10 and 30 has one additional reading of 385 appended. Which statement best describes the effect on the mean and the median?
choices: Neither statistic changes, because one value cannot affect a summary.
Both the mean and the median rise sharply.
The median rises sharply while the mean changes little.
The mean rises sharply while the median changes little, because the mean uses every value’s size.

A least-squares line for a data set is ŷ = 15x + 5, where x is measured in kilometre travelleds and y in litres of fuel. Interpret the slope.
choices: Each additional kilometre travelled causes an increase of exactly 15 litres of fuel.
Each additional kilometre travelled is associated with an increase of about 15 litres of fuel.
Each additional litres of fuel is associated with 15 more kilometre travelleds.
The predicted value is 15 litres of fuel when x is 0.
